title: Trying to fake dynamic 3D lighting on hand-painted 2D assets. What breaks the illusion?
author: Kiko_Production
selftext:
Still experimenting with the lighting system for my city builder.

The buildings and environment are mostly 2D assets, but I’m using normal maps, directional shadows and emissive windows to make them react to the time of day.

I also reworked the environment and buildings after the feedback on my previous test.

What’s the first thing that looks “off” to you lighting, shadows, scale, or the assets themselves?

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
The lighting is great for the style. Nothing is 'wrong' with this per se. The only suggestions I have are:

1. The garbage can looking thing next to the building in the bottom right is a bit weird to my eye, as I don't really know what it is and so my brain just associates the one thing it does pair that shape with. But I assume it's just something I'm unfamiliar with.

2. Houses themselves seem small, considering the size of the doors vs the size of the buildings.

3. While the quality of the lighting is solid, the actual liveliness of the scene is less so. Games generally address this through visible wind, foliage or creature activity, cloud shadows paired with world light (moon or sun, depending), or simple prop idle animations like some light flickering, etc.

Nothing wrong with what you've got though. Just if you wanted to expand on it, those are possible directions to pursue.

replies.author: Kiko_Production
replies.body:
Thanks, this is really useful feedback! That “trash can” is actually meant to be a water tank, so I clearly need to work on its silhouette and make its connection to the pump more obvious 😅

Good catch on the proportions too I’ll revisit the door sizes relative to the houses.

There’s already some wind, chimney smoke, and moving cloud shadows, but they may be too subtle at this viewing distance. Your point about the scene needing more visible life makes sense. 

Glad the lighting feels right for the style!

I’m also planning to add little townspeople walking around the city, which should help make it feel more alive and give a clearer sense of scale.

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body:
Yeah I kind of figured you just hadn't gotten to some of that stuff yet. And yes maybe make those things a bit less subtle, as I didn't even see the chimney smoke. I see the trees shifting but I meant more like visible wind gusts (although it's possible those are there too but the speed is making them hard to process?)

I'm not entirely sure what  you're going for with the game's genre/gameplay/etc, but even not knowing that, I'll say this gives me Project Zomboid vibes IF that game was more visually polished/consistent. So it's a solid direction.

replies.author: Kiko_Production
replies.body: It’s an isometric city-building/management game, so it’s encouraging that the visual direction comes across well. The clip was sped up 24×, which probably made the ambient motion harder to read. Your distinction between swaying trees and visible gusts is helpful. I will work on making more readable smoke and coordinated wind movement

comments.author: heavy-minium
comments.body:
Ambient occlusion, even if faked, would do wonders here. Even at night, when a global light does "moonlight" lighting.

Would help making the buildings more "grounded" into environment.

replies.author: Kiko_Production
replies.body: Good point! There’s already some contact shading, but it’s too weak and doesn’t follow the building foundations closely enough. I’m improving that so the buildings feel more grounded during both day and night

comments.author: Old-Wolverine-4134
comments.body: Even at night you have to have shadows because it's not completely dark, you have light source (lights, moon, etc).

comments.author: Youriberg
comments.body: shadows should be less blurred as the general artistic style is not blurring compatible I would say or at least not the way it's done currently.

comments.author: Jolly-Rip5973
comments.body: that's honestly good enough. Looks pretty good.

comments.author: IndividualBass83
comments.body: Very cool tho, love the style. Its good enough, don't go crazy on the very small details!
